=== /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/835_build_quotes_with_per-room_per-sqft_or_hourly_pricing/criterion_7112_owner_builds_a_per-room_quote_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7112Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7112 — Owner builds a per-room quote: selecting the per-room
  pricing model and entering room counts prices the quote per room, and
  no square-footage or hourly inputs are ever requested alongside it.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "owner builds a per-room quote" do
    scenario "the quote is priced per room with no square-footage or hourly inputs requested" do
      given_ "the owner is creating a new quote for a lead", context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the owner selects the per-room pricing model and adds 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms",
            context do
        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
            quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 3, bathroom_count: 2}
          )
          |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the quote is priced per room and no square-footage or hourly inputs are requested",
            context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='room-bedroom-count-input']")
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='room-bathroom-count-input']")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='square-feet-input']")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='hours-input']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

=== /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/835_build_quotes_with_per-room_per-sqft_or_hourly_pricing/criterion_7114_switching_pricing_model_clears_the_other_models_inputs_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7114Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7114 — Switching pricing model clears the other model's
  inputs: a quote is priced by exactly one model at a time, so changing
  the model wipes out line items that belonged to the previous model.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "switching pricing model clears the other model's inputs" do
    scenario "per-room line items are cleared and the quote is priced only on hours" do
      given_ "the owner has started a per-room quote with rooms entered", context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
          quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 3, bathroom_count: 1}
        )
        |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the owner switches the pricing model to hourly", context do
        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> form("[data-test='quote-form']", quote: %{pricing_model: "hourly"})
          |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the per-room line items are cleared and the quote is priced only on hours, never a mix of both models",
            context do
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='room-bedroom-count-input']")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='room-bathroom-count-input']")
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='hours-input']")
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$0.00")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7119Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7119 — Owner quotes a phone lead without visiting the
  property: a quote can be built and sent entirely from client-supplied
  details, with no in-person walkthrough required first.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "owner quotes a phone lead without visiting the property" do
    scenario "a complete priced quote is sent without scheduling a site visit" do
      given_ "a lead has given the owner their room count and square footage over the phone",
             context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='rate-card-form']",
          rate_card: %{per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 5000, per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3000}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the owner builds a quote entering those details from their device", context do
        context.quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
          quote: %{
            client_name: "Dana Prescott",
            client_phone: "555-0142",
            pricing_model: "per_room",
            bedroom_count: 3,
            bathroom_count: 1
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        context.quote_live
        |> element("[data-test='send-quote-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner can produce and send a complete priced quote without scheduling a site visit",
            context do
        path = assert_patch(context.quote_live)
        {:ok, sent_live, html} = live(context.conn, path)

        assert html =~ "$180.00"
        assert has_element?(sent_live, "[data-test='quote-status']", "Sent")
        refute html =~ "Schedule a site visit"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7120Spex do

  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7120 — Missing rate on the chosen model blocks finalizing:

    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}

    scenario "finalizing is blocked and the owner is prompted to set the missing rate" do
      given_ "the owner's rate card has no rate configured for the hourly model", context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

44	  """

46	    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
47	  end

50	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
51	    client
52	    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
53	    |> Repo.update()
54	  end

66

69	  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
70	  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
71	  """

    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists only active clients, for the account's day-to-day client list.
  """
  def list_active_clients(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
  end

  def update_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    client
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def deactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => false})
  end

  def reactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => true})
  end

  @doc """
  Permanently deletes a client and its properties.

  Refuses to delete a client that still has dependent records (e.g.
  scheduled jobs) elsewhere in the system — the database's foreign key
  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
  """
  def delete_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.delete(client)
  rescue
    Ecto.ConstraintError -> {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs}
  end

  ## Properties

  @doc """
  Lists a client's properties, ordered by address.
  """
  def list_properties(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{id: client_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id and p.client_id == ^client_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries recorded against a property, most recent first.
  """
  def list_property_audit_entries(%Scope{} = scope, %Property{} = property) do
    Recorder.list_for_subject(scope, "Property", property.id)
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry do
  @moduledoc """
  An immutable record of actor, action, subject, and old/new values.

  Append-only: no update or delete function is exposed anywhere in the
  codebase, and the `audit_entries` table itself has DB rules blocking
  UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth (see the migration that created it).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          actor_id: integer() | nil,
          system: boolean(),
          action: String.t() | nil,
          subject_type: String.t() | nil,
          subject_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          old_value: map(),
          new_value: map(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "audit_entries" do
    field :system, :boolean, default: false
    field :action, :string
    field :subject_type, :string
    field :subject_id, Ecto.UUID
    field :old_value, :map, default: %{}
    field :new_value, :map, default: %{}

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :actor, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
  end

  def changeset(entry, attrs) do
    entry
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :account_id,
      :actor_id,
      :system,
      :action,
      :subject_type,
      :subject_id,
      :old_value,
      :new_value
    ])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :action, :subject_type, :subject_id])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder do
  @moduledoc """
  API other contexts call to append audit trail entries.

  Callers pass the acting scope, an action string, the subject being
  changed, and old/new value maps. Nothing here ever updates or deletes
  a row — this module only ever inserts.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Records an audit entry attributed to the scope's current user.
  """
  def record(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        action,
        subject_type,
        subject_id,
        old_value \\ %{},
        new_value \\ %{}
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(action) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    %AuditEntry{}
    |> AuditEntry.changeset(%{
      account_id: account_id,
      actor_id: scope.user && scope.user.id,
      system: false,
      action: action,
      subject_type: subject_type,
      subject_id: subject_id,
      old_value: old_value,
      new_value: new_value
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries for a subject, most recent first.
  """
  def list_for_subject(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, subject_type, subject_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where(
      [e],
      e.account_id == ^account_id and e.subject_type == ^subject_type and
        e.subject_id == ^subject_id
    )
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end
end

  @moduledoc """
  This module defines test helpers for creating
  entities via the `CleanerCrm.Users` context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def unique_user_email, do: "user#{System.unique_integer()}@example.com"
  def valid_user_password, do: "hello world!"

  def valid_user_attributes(attrs \\ %{}) do
    Enum.into(attrs, %{
      email: unique_user_email()
    })
  end

  def unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, user} =
      attrs
      |> valid_user_attributes()
      |> Users.register_user()

    user
  end

  def user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs)

    token =
      extract_user_token(fn url ->
        Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, url)
      end)

    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

    user
  end

  def user_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    user_scope_fixture(user)
  end

  def user_scope_fixture(user) do
    Scope.for_user(user)
  end

  def set_password(user) do
    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

  def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

  def override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) when is_binary(token) do
    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(t in Users.UserToken,
        where: t.token == ^token
      ),
      set: [authenticated_at: authenticated_at]
    )
  end

  def generate_user_magic_link_token(user) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = Users.UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    CleanerCrm.Repo.insert!(user_token)
    {encoded_token, user_token.token}
  end

  def offset_user_token(token, amount_to_add, unit) do
    dt = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(:second), amount_to_add, unit)

    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(ut in Users.UserToken, where: ut.token == ^token),
      set: [inserted_at: dt, authenticated_at: dt]
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
    else
      conn
    end
  end

  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #
  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do

    else

  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #

  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do

# Money Handling — integer cents, no money library

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Quotes (835), invoices/payments (836), and pay/earnings (838, 844) all handle money. Research shows pay-transparency disputes are a core cleaner pain, so amounts must never drift from float arithmetic. The product is US-only, USD-only at MVP.

## Options Considered

- **Integer cents in Postgres** — exact, simple, matches Stripe's amount convention.
- **ex_money** — multi-currency correctness we don't need; adds a dependency and custom Ecto types.
- **Decimal columns** — exact but invites fractional-cent ambiguity in piece-rate math.

## Decision

Store all monetary amounts as integer cents (`:integer` columns, `_cents` suffix). Rate math (per-sqft, hourly proration) computes in `Decimal` and rounds half-up to cents at each persisted boundary. A small `CleanerCrm.Money` formatting helper renders `$X.XX`; Stripe amounts pass through unchanged.

## Consequences

- Multi-currency would require a migration to ex_money later; acceptable for a US-market MVP.
- Rounding policy (half-up at persistence boundaries) must be stated in Quoting and TimeTracking specs so earnings and invoice totals always reconcile.

# Audit Trail — project-local append-only audit table

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Story 840: owners want to see who changed what and when (a direct MaidCentral user wish), including attributing automated recurring-job generation to the system. Entries must be immutable (criterion 7198) and filterable.

## Options Considered

- **Project-local `audit_entries` table + `Audit.Recorder`** — explicit, scoped to the events that matter, easy to attribute system actors.
- **paper_trail / ex_audit** — generic row-versioning; captures noise, awkward system-actor attribution, and both are lightly maintained.
- **Postgres triggers** — invisible to application code and hard to attribute to the acting user.

## Decision

Write a project-local `CleanerCrm.Audit` context: an append-only `audit_entries` table (actor_id nullable + `system` flag, action, subject type/id, old/new value maps as JSONB, company-scoped) with a `Recorder` API called explicitly from mutating context functions. No update/delete functions are exposed; a DB rule/constraint blocks UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth.

## Consequences

- Explicit call sites mean a mutation can forget to record; Credo local check or code review must watch for this in mutating context functions.
- JSONB old/new maps keep the schema stable as audited entities evolve.
- Retention/archival policy deferred until data volume warrants it.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->

  @moduledoc """
  CleanerCrm keeps the contexts that define your domain
  and business logic.

  Contexts are also responsible for managing your data, regardless

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.FormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create/edit a client's name and billing preference. On successful save, navigates to the client's own page directly (rather than notifying the parent to do it) — a parent's `handle_info` reacting to a component's self-sent message runs one mailbox message after the "save" event's own reply, too late for `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_submit/1` to observe the redirect. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|---------------|----------|----------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :edit` | yes | which mode the form is in | | client | `Client.t()` | yes | `%Client{}` (blank for `:new`, loaded for `:edit`) | ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Clients` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Clients @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header>{form_title(@action)} <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="client-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:name]} type="text" label="Name" /> <.input field={@form[:card_on_file]} type="checkbox" label="Card on file" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Client
""" end @impl true def update(%{client: client} = assigns, socket) do changeset = Clients.change_client(assigns.current_scope, client) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset))} end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"client" => client_params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Clients.change_client(socket.assigns.client, client_params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end def handle_event("save", %{"client" => client_params}, socket) do save_client(socket, socket.assigns.action, client_params) end defp save_client(socket, :new, params) do case Clients.create_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, client} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/clients/#{client}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp save_client(socket, :edit, params) do case Clients.update_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.client, params) do {:ok, client} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/clients/#{client}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp form_title(:new), do: "New Client" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Client" end

Deleting a client is refused when the database reports dependent records elsewhere (e.g. scheduled jobs) — this module doesn't know or care what those dependents are, only that the delete was rejected. ## Routes * `/clients/:id` (`:show`) and `/clients/:id/edit` (`:edit`) — the client and its properties. * `/clients/:id/properties/new` (`:new_client_property`) and `/properties/new` (`:new_property`) — add a property, with or without a preselected client. * `/properties/:id` (`:show_property`) and `/properties/:id/edit` (`:edit_property`) — a single property's access details and change history. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Clients` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Clients alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property alias CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.{FormComponent, PropertyFormComponent} @impl true def render(%{live_action: action} = assigns) when action in [:show, :edit] do ~H""" <.header> {@client.name} <:subtitle :if={!@client.active}>Inactive <:actions> <.button navigate={~p"/clients/#{@client}/edit"} class="btn-sm btn-ghost">Edit <.button :if={@client.active} phx-click="deactivate-client" data-test="deactivate-client-button" data-confirm="Deactivate this client?" class="btn-sm" > Deactivate <.button :if={!@client.active} phx-click="reactivate-client" class="btn-sm"> Reactivate <.button phx-click="delete-client" data-test="delete-client-button" data-confirm="Permanently delete this client?" class="btn-sm btn-error" > Delete
<.live_component module={FormComponent} id="client-form" current_scope={@current_scope} action={:edit} client={@client} />
<.header> Properties <:actions> <.button navigate={~p"/clients/#{@client}/properties/new"} class="btn-sm"> <.icon name="hero-plus" class="size-4 mr-1" /> Add Property

No properties yet.

  • <.link navigate={~p"/properties/#{property}"} class="font-semibold link"> {property.service_address}
""" end def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header>{property_header(@live_action, assigns)} <.live_component :if={@live_action in [:new_client_property, :new_property, :edit_property]} module={PropertyFormComponent} id="property-form" current_scope={@current_scope} action={property_form_action(@live_action)} client={@client} property={@property} />

Client: <.link navigate={~p"/clients/#{@client}"} data-test="property-client" class="link font-semibold" > {@client.name}

Entry method: {@property.entry_method}

Lockbox code: {@property.lockbox_code}

Alarm code: {@property.alarm_code}

Parking notes: {@property.parking_notes}

Pet notes: {@property.pet_notes}

Emergency contact: {@property.emergency_contact_name} {@property.emergency_contact_phone}

<.button navigate={~p"/properties/#{@property}/edit"} class="btn-sm"> Edit Property
<.header>Access Change History

No changes recorded yet.

  • {entry.actor && entry.actor.email} changed {changed_fields_text(entry)}

    {DateTime.to_iso8601(entry.inserted_at)}

""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket), do: {:ok, socket} @impl true def handle_params(params, _url, socket) do {:noreply, apply_action(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, params)} end defp apply_action(socket, :show, %{"id" => id}) do client = Clients.get_client!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id) socket |> assign(:page_title, client.name) |> assign(:client, client) |> assign(:properties, Clients.list_properties(socket.assigns.current_scope, client)) end defp apply_action(socket, :edit, %{"id" => id}) do socket = apply_action(socket, :show, %{"id" => id}) assign(socket, :page_title, "Edit #{socket.assigns.client.name}") end defp apply_action(socket, :new_client_property, %{"id" => id}) do client = Clients.get_client!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id) socket |> assign(:page_title, "New Property") |> assign(:client, client) |> assign(:property, %Property{}) end defp apply_action(socket, :new_property, _params) do socket |> assign(:page_title, "New Property") |> assign(:client, nil) |> assign(:property, %Property{}) end defp apply_action(socket, :show_property, %{"id" => id}) do property = Clients.get_property!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id) client = Clients.get_client!(socket.assigns.current_scope, property.client_id) socket |> assign(:page_title, property.service_address) |> assign(:property, property) |> assign(:client, client) |> assign( :audit_entries, Clients.list_property_audit_entries(socket.assigns.current_scope, property) ) end defp apply_action(socket, :edit_property, %{"id" => id}) do property = Clients.get_property!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id) client = Clients.get_client!(socket.assigns.current_scope, property.client_id) socket |> assign(:page_title, "Edit Property") |> assign(:property, property) |> assign(:client, client) end @impl true def handle_event("deactivate-client", _params, socket) do {:ok, client} = Clients.deactivate_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.client) {:noreply, assign(socket, :client, client)} end def handle_event("reactivate-client", _params, socket) do {:ok, client} = Clients.reactivate_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.client) {:noreply, assign(socket, :client, client)} end def handle_event("delete-client", _params, socket) do case Clients.delete_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.client) do {:ok, _client} -> {:noreply, socket |> put_flash(:info, "Client deleted successfully") |> push_navigate(to: ~p"/clients")} {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs} -> {:noreply, put_flash( socket, :error, "This client has upcoming jobs. Please deactivate it or remove the upcoming jobs before deleting." )} end end @impl true def handle_info({PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, property}}, socket) do {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/properties/#{property}")} end defp property_header(:new_client_property, %{client: client}), do: "New Property for #{client.name}" defp property_header(:new_property, _assigns), do: "New Property" defp property_header(:edit_property, %{property: property}), do: "Edit #{property.service_address}" defp property_header(:show_property, %{property: property}), do: property.service_address defp property_form_action(:edit_property), do: :edit defp property_form_action(_), do: :new defp changed_fields_text(%{new_value: %{"changed_fields" => fields}}) when is_list(fields) do fields |> Enum.map(&String.replace(&1, "_", " ")) |> Enum.join(", ") end defp changed_fields_text(_entry), do: "access details" end

attr :variant, :string, values: ~w(primary)
  slot :inner_block, required: true

  def button(%{rest: rest} = assigns) do
    variants = %{"primary" => "btn-primary", nil => "btn-primary btn-soft"}

    assigns =
      assign_new(assigns, :class, fn ->
        ["btn", Map.fetch!(variants, assigns[:variant])]
      end)

    if rest[:href] || rest[:navigate] || rest[:patch] do
      ~H"""
      <.link class={@class} {@rest}>
        {render_slot(@inner_block)}
      </.link>
      """
    else
      ~H"""
      <button class={@class} {@rest}>
        {render_slot(@inner_block)}
      </button>
      """
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Renders an input with label and error messages.

  A `Phoenix.HTML.FormField` may be passed as argument,
  which is used to retrieve the input name, id, and values.
  Otherwise all attributes may be passed explicitly.

  ## Types

  This function accepts all HTML input types, considering that:

    * You may also set `type="select"` to render a `<select>` tag

    * `type="checkbox"` is used exclusively to render boolean values

defmodule CleanerCrm.Money do
  @moduledoc """
  Formats integer cents for display, per the money-handling ADR: every
  amount is stored and computed as integer cents, and this is the only
  place a dollar string gets built.
  """

  @doc """
  Formats integer cents as `"$X.XX"`, with thousands separators. `nil`
  is treated as zero.

  ## Examples

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(18_000)
      "$180.00"

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(nil)
      "$0.00"
  """
  @spec format_cents(integer() | nil) :: String.t()
  def format_cents(nil), do: format_cents(0)

  def format_cents(cents) when is_integer(cents) do
    sign = if cents < 0, do: "-", else: ""
    dollars = div(abs(cents), 100)
    remainder = rem(abs(cents), 100)

    "#{sign}$#{group_thousands(dollars)}.#{pad_cents(remainder)}"
  end

  defp pad_cents(remainder), do: remainder |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")

  defp group_thousands(dollars) do
    dollars
    |> Integer.to_string()
    |> String.reverse()
    |> String.replace(~r/(\d{3})(?=\d)/, "\\1,")
    |> String.reverse()
  end
end

  ## Examples

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(18_000)
      "$180.00"

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(nil)
      "$0.00"

  @spec format_cents(integer() | nil) :: String.t()
  def format_cents(nil), do: format_cents(0)

  def format_cents(cents) when is_integer(cents) do
    sign = if cents < 0, do: "-", else: ""
    dollars = div(abs(cents), 100)
    remainder = rem(abs(cents), 100)

    "#{sign}$#{group_thousands(dollars)}.#{pad_cents(remainder)}"
  end

  defp pad_cents(remainder), do: remainder |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")

  defp group_thousands(dollars) do
    dollars
    |> Integer.to_string()
    |> String.reverse()
    |> String.replace(~r/(\d{3})(?=\d)/, "\\1,")
    |> String.reverse()
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Computes a quote's line items and total from a rate card, and decides
  whether a quote is ready to send.

  Pure and side-effect free: it never touches the database, so
  `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.Builder` can call it on every keystroke for
  live totals, and `CleanerCrm.Quoting.send_quote/3` can call it again
  at the moment of persistence.

  Per the money-handling ADR, rate math is done in `Decimal` and
  rounded half-up to whole cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, RateCard}

  @type line_item :: %{
          description: String.t(),
          quantity: integer(),
          rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer()
        }

  @doc """
  The quote form field names (as submitted param keys) that belong to
  a given pricing model — used to drop inputs left over from a
  previously selected model when the owner switches models.
  """
  @spec fields_for_model(String.t()) :: [String.t()]
  def fields_for_model("per_room"), do: ~w(bedroom_count bathroom_count)
  def fields_for_model("per_sqft"), do: ~w(square_feet)
  def fields_for_model("hourly"), do: ~w(hours)
  def fields_for_model(_other), do: []

  @doc """
  The priced line items for a quote's chosen model. Only items with a
  positive quantity are included — an empty or zero field never
  demands a rate. A `nil` `rate_cents` means the rate card has nothing
  configured yet for that item, and its amount is zero.
  """
  @spec line_items(RateCard.t(), Quote.t()) :: [line_item()]
  def line_items(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Quote{} = quote) do
    quote.pricing_model
    |> model_items(rate_card, quote)
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.quantity > 0))
  end

  defp model_items(:per_room, rate_card, quote) do
    [
      item("Bedrooms", quote.bedroom_count, rate_card.per_room_bedroom_rate_cents),
      item("Bathrooms", quote.bathroom_count, rate_card.per_room_bathroom_rate_cents)
    ]
  end

  defp model_items(:per_sqft, rate_card, quote) do
    [item("Square footage", quote.square_feet, rate_card.per_sqft_rate_cents)]
  end

  defp model_items(:hourly, rate_card, quote) do
    [item("Hours", quote.hours, rate_card.hourly_rate_cents)]
  end

  defp model_items(nil, _rate_card, _quote), do: []

  defp item(description, quantity, rate_cents) do
    quantity = quantity || 0

    %{
      description: description,
      quantity: quantity,
      rate_cents: rate_cents,
      amount_cents: amount_cents(quantity, rate_cents)
    }
  end

  defp amount_cents(quantity, rate_cents)
       when is_integer(quantity) and is_integer(rate_cents) and quantity > 0 do
    quantity
    |> Decimal.new()
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.new(rate_cents))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end

  defp amount_cents(_quantity, _rate_cents), do: 0

  @doc "Sums a quote's line items into its total, in cents."
  @spec total_cents([line_item()]) :: integer()
  def total_cents(line_items), do: Enum.reduce(line_items, 0, &(&1.amount_cents + &2))

  @doc "Whether any priced line item is missing a rate from the rate card."
  @spec missing_rate?([line_item()]) :: boolean()
  def missing_rate?(line_items), do: Enum.any?(line_items, &is_nil(&1.rate_cents))

  @doc """
  Whether a quote is ready to send: at least one priced line item,
  every one of them rated, and a positive total.
  """
  @spec finalizable?([line_item()]) :: boolean()
  def finalizable?(line_items) do
    line_items != [] and not missing_rate?(line_items) and total_cents(line_items) > 0
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting do
  @moduledoc """
  Quotes built from the account's rate card using per-room, per-sqft,
  or hourly pricing models.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. A quote is
  built up in memory (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`) and only ever
  persisted at the moment it's sent — `send_quote/3` freezes the rate
  card's current rates into the quote's line items, so later rate-card
  edits never alter an already-sent quote.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, QuoteItem, RateCard, Pricing}

  ## Rate card

  @doc """
  Returns the account's rate card, creating a blank one on first use.
  """
  def get_or_create_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(RateCard, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> Repo.insert!(%RateCard{account_id: account_id})
      rate_card -> rate_card
    end

  def change_rate_card(%Scope{}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs \\ %{}) do

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.Builder do @moduledoc """ Builds and sends a quote, with live totals as the owner fills it in. The rate card and quote forms live on the same page: a quote is priced by exactly one model at a time, so switching models drops whatever the previous model's inputs held (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing.fields_for_model/1`). A quote is only ever persisted at the moment it's sent — before that, everything here is in-memory socket state. ## Routes * `/quotes/new` (`:new`) — build and send a new quote. * `/quotes/:id` (`:show`) — a previously sent quote, frozen against later rate-card changes. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Quoting` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Quoting alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Pricing, Quote} @impl true def render(%{live_action: :show} = assigns) do ~H""" <.header> {@quote.client_name || "Unnamed lead"} <:subtitle>{pricing_model_label(@quote.pricing_model)} quote <:actions> <.button navigate={~p"/quotes"} class="btn-sm btn-ghost">Back to Quotes

Status: {status_label(@quote.status)}

Phone: {@quote.client_phone}

  • {item.description} × {item.quantity} @ {Money.format_cents(item.rate_cents)}
    {Money.format_cents(item.amount_cents)}

Total: {Money.format_cents(@quote.total_cents)}

""" end def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> New Quote <:subtitle>Price a job by room, square footage, or hours

Rate Card

<.form for={@rate_card_form} id="rate-card-form" data-test="rate-card-form" phx-submit="save_rate_card" > <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_room_bedroom_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-bedroom rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_room_bathroom_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-bathroom rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_sqft_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-square-foot rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:hourly_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Hourly rate (cents)" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Rate Card

Quote Details

<.form for={@form} id="quote-form" data-test="quote-form" phx-change="validate" phx-submit="validate" > <.input field={@form[:client_name]} type="text" label="Client name" /> <.input field={@form[:client_phone]} type="text" label="Client phone" /> <.input field={@form[:pricing_model]} type="select" label="Pricing model" prompt="Select a pricing model" options={[ {"Per room", :per_room}, {"Per square foot", :per_sqft}, {"Hourly", :hourly} ]} />
<.input field={@form[:bedroom_count]} type="number" label="Bedrooms" data-test="room-bedroom-count-input" /> <.input field={@form[:bathroom_count]} type="number" label="Bathrooms" data-test="room-bathroom-count-input" />
<.input :if={@pricing_model == :per_sqft} field={@form[:square_feet]} type="number" label="Square feet" data-test="square-feet-input" /> <.input :if={@pricing_model == :hourly} field={@form[:hours]} type="number" label="Hours" data-test="hours-input" />

Total: {Money.format_cents(@total_cents)}

Add a rate for this pricing model on your rate card before sending this quote.

<.button type="button" phx-click="send_quote" data-test="send-quote-button" variant="primary" > Send Quote
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket), do: {:ok, socket} @impl true def handle_params(params, _url, socket) do {:noreply, apply_action(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, params)} end defp apply_action(socket, :new, _params) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope rate_card = Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope) changeset = Quoting.change_quote(scope, %Quote{}) socket |> assign(:page_title, "New Quote") |> assign(:rate_card, rate_card) |> assign(:rate_card_form, to_form(Quoting.change_rate_card(scope, rate_card))) |> recalculate(changeset) end defp apply_action(socket, :show, %{"id" => id}) do quote = Quoting.get_quote!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id) socket |> assign(:page_title, quote.client_name || "Quote") |> assign(:quote, quote) end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"quote" => quote_params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Quoting.change_quote(%Quote{}, sanitize_quote_params(quote_params)) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, recalculate(socket, changeset)} end def handle_event("save_rate_card", %{"rate_card" => rate_card_params}, socket) do %{current_scope: scope, rate_card: rate_card, form: form} = socket.assigns case Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, rate_card, rate_card_params) do {:ok, rate_card} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:rate_card, rate_card) |> assign(:rate_card_form, to_form(Quoting.change_rate_card(scope, rate_card))) |> recalculate(form.source)} {:error, changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :rate_card_form, to_form(changeset))} end end def handle_event("send_quote", _params, socket) do %{current_scope: scope, quote_draft: draft, rate_card: rate_card} = socket.assigns case Quoting.send_quote(scope, draft, rate_card) do {:ok, quote} -> {:noreply, push_patch(socket, to: ~p"/quotes/#{quote}")} {:error, :not_finalizable} -> {:noreply, socket} end end defp recalculate(socket, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset) do quote_draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) line_items = Pricing.line_items(socket.assigns.rate_card, quote_draft) socket |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset)) |> assign(:quote_draft, quote_draft) |> assign(:pricing_model, quote_draft.pricing_model) |> assign(:total_cents, Pricing.total_cents(line_items)) |> assign(:missing_rate?, Pricing.missing_rate?(line_items)) end defp sanitize_quote_params(%{"pricing_model" => model} = params) do Map.take(params, ["client_name", "client_phone", "pricing_model" | Pricing.fields_for_model(model)]) end defp sanitize_quote_params(params), do: Map.take(params, ~w(client_name client_phone pricing_model)) defp pricing_model_label(:per_room), do: "Per room" defp pricing_model_label(:per_sqft), do: "Per square foot" defp pricing_model_label(:hourly), do: "Hourly" defp pricing_model_label(nil), do: "Unpriced" defp status_label(:draft), do: "Draft" defp status_label(:sent), do: "Sent" end

-> {:noreply, push_patch(socket, to: ~p"/quotes/#{quote}")} {:error, :not_finalizable} -> {:noreply, socket} end end defp recalculate(socket, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset) do quote_draft = content.content:
mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

## Examples

    mix spex
    mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
    mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
    mix spex --verbose
    mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
    mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
    mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
    mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
    mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
    mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests

defmodule CleanerCrm.Repo.Migrations.AddTimeTrackingPayFields do
  use Ecto.Migration

  # Additive columns only — `jobs` and `accounts` stay owned by
  # Scheduling/Accounts, but a job's pay arrangement and an account's
  # drive-time policy are read and written by TimeTracking (the same
  # relationship `agreed_price_cents` already has with Billing).
  def change do
    alter table(:jobs) do
      add :pay_type, :string
      add :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
      add :piece_rate_cents, :integer
    end

    alter table(:accounts) do
      add :drive_time_policy, :string, null: false, default: "unpaid"
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Repo.Migrations.CreateQualityTables do
  use Ecto.Migration

  def change do
    create table(:checklist_templates, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :property_id, references(:properties, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :nilify_all)
      add :name, :string, null: false
      add :items, {:array, :map}, null: false, default: []

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
    end

    create index(:checklist_templates, [:account_id])
    create index(:checklist_templates, [:property_id])

    create table(:checklists, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :job_id, references(:jobs, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all), null: false

      add :checklist_template_id,
          references(:checklist_templates, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :nilify_all)

      add :owner_rating, :integer
      add :quality_score, :float
      add :completed_at, :utc_datetime_usec

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
    end

    create index(:checklists, [:account_id])
    create unique_index(:checklists, [:job_id])
    create index(:checklists, [:checklist_template_id])

    create table(:checklist_items, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :checklist_id, references(:checklists, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :room, :string
      add :task, :string, null: false
      add :required, :boolean, null: false, default: true
      add :checked, :boolean, null: false, default: false
      add :checked_at, :utc_datetime_usec
      add :skipped, :boolean, null: false, default: false
      add :skip_reason, :string
      add :position, :integer, null: false, default: 0

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
    end

    create index(:checklist_items, [:checklist_id])

    create table(:incident_reports, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :job_id, references(:jobs, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all), null: false
      add :cleaner_id, references(:users, on_delete: :nilify_all)
      add :type, :string, null: false
      add :description, :text, null: false
      add :filed_at, :utc_datetime_usec, null: false

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
    end

    create index(:incident_reports, [:account_id])
    create index(:incident_reports, [:job_id])

    # Defense in depth: incident reports are append-only. Application
    # code never exposes update/delete; these rules block it even if
    # it did.
    execute(
      "CREATE RULE incident_reports_no_update AS ON UPDATE TO incident_reports DO INSTEAD NOTHING",
      "DROP RULE IF EXISTS incident_reports_no_update ON incident_reports"
    )

    execute(
      "CREATE RULE incident_reports_no_delete AS ON DELETE TO incident_reports DO INSTEAD NOTHING",
      "DROP RULE IF EXISTS incident_reports_no_delete ON incident_reports"
    )

    create table(:photos, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :checklist_item_id,
          references(:checklist_items, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all)

      add :incident_report_id,
          references(:incident_reports, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all)

      add :kind, :string, null: false
      add :upload_state, :string, null: false, default: "pending"
      add :storage_key, :string
      add :captured_at, :utc_datetime_usec

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
    end

    create index(:photos, [:account_id])
    create index(:photos, [:checklist_item_id])
    create index(:photos, [:incident_report_id])
  end
end

  defp maybe_values(type, root, {tag, _, _} = node, element)
       when type in [:change, :submit] do
    cond do
      tag == "form" ->
        value_inputs = DOM.all_value_inputs(node, root)
        defaults = DOM.collect_form_values(node, root, fn defaults -> defaults end)

        lazy_submitter =
          case TreeDOM.attribute(node, "id") do
            nil ->
              # to collect the submitter by selector,
              # need to convert the tree to a lazy here :(
              fn -> DOM.to_lazy([node]) end

              # a lazy function that returns a lazy node with all form inputs
              # that could be the submitter to collect the submitter by selector
              fn -> DOM.all(root, ~s<
                ##{id} :is(input, button):not([form]:not([form="#{id}"])),
                :is(input, button)[form="#{id}"]
              >) end
          end

        with {:ok, defaults} <-
               maybe_submitter(defaults, type, lazy_submitter, element),
             {:ok, value} <-
               fill_in_map(Enum.to_list(element.form_data || %{}), "", value_inputs, []) do
          {:ok,
           defaults
           |> Query.decode_done()
           |> deep_merge(TreeDOM.all_values(node))
           |> deep_merge(value)}
        else

        end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.Builder do @moduledoc """ Builds and sends a quote, with live totals as the owner fills it in. The rate card and quote forms live on the same page: a quote is priced by exactly one model at a time, so switching models drops whatever the previous model's inputs held (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing.fields_for_model/1`). A quote is only ever persisted at the moment it's sent — before that, everything here is in-memory socket state. ## Routes * `/quotes/new` (`:new`) — build and send a new quote. * `/quotes/:id` (`:show`) — a previously sent quote, frozen against later rate-card changes. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Quoting` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Quoting alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Pricing, Quote} @impl true def render(%{live_action: :show} = assigns) do ~H""" <.header> {@quote.client_name || "Unnamed lead"} <:subtitle>{pricing_model_label(@quote.pricing_model)} quote <:actions> <.button navigate={~p"/quotes"} class="btn-sm btn-ghost">Back to Quotes

Status: {status_label(@quote.status)}

Phone: {@quote.client_phone}

  • {item.description} × {item.quantity} @ {Money.format_cents(item.rate_cents)}
    {Money.format_cents(item.amount_cents)}

Total: {Money.format_cents(@quote.total_cents)}

""" end def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> New Quote <:subtitle>Price a job by room, square footage, or hours

Rate Card

<.form for={@rate_card_form} id="rate-card-form" data-test="rate-card-form" phx-submit="save_rate_card" > <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_room_bedroom_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-bedroom rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_room_bathroom_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-bathroom rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:per_sqft_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Per-square-foot rate (cents)" /> <.input field={@rate_card_form[:hourly_rate_cents]} type="number" label="Hourly rate (cents)" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Rate Card

Quote Details

<.input field={@form[:bedroom_count]} type="number" label="Bedrooms" data-test="room-bedroom-count-input" /> <.input field={@form[:bathroom_count]} type="number" label="Bathrooms" data-test="room-bathroom-count-input" />
<.input :if={@pricing_model == :per_sqft} field={@form[:square_feet]} type="number" label="Square feet" data-test="square-feet-input" /> <.input :if={@pricing_model == :hourly} field={@form[:hours]} type="number" label="Hours" data-test="hours-input" />

Total: {Money.format_cents(@total_cents)}

Add a rate for this pricing model on your rate card before sending this quote.

<.button type="button" phx-click="send_quote" data-test="send-quote-button" variant="primary" > Send Quote
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket), do: {:ok, socket} @impl true def handle_params(params, _url, socket) do {:noreply, apply_action(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, params)}   def handle_event("send_quote", _params, socket) do
    %{current_scope: scope, quote_draft: draft, rate_card: rate_card} = socket.assigns

    case Quoting.send_quote(scope, draft, rate_card) do
      {:ok, quote} -> {:noreply, push_patch(socket, to: ~p"/quotes/#{quote}")}
      {:error, :not_finalizable} -> {:noreply, socket}
    end

  defp recalculate(socket, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset) do
    quote_draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset)
    line_items = Pricing.line_items(socket.assigns.rate_card, quote_draft)

    socket
    |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset))
    |> assign(:quote_draft, quote_draft)
    |> assign(:pricing_model, quote_draft.pricing_model)
    |> assign(:total_cents, Pricing.total_cents(line_items))
    |> assign(:missing_rate?, Pricing.missing_rate?(line_items))
  end

    Map.take(params, [
      "client_name",

      "pricing_model" | Pricing.fields_for_model(model)

Files: lib/cleaner_crm/quoting.ex, quoting/{quote,quote_item,rate_card,pricing}.ex, lib/cleaner_crm/money.ex, priv/repo/migrations/20260707200099_create_quoting_tables.exs, lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/quote_live/{index,builder}.ex, plus additive edits to lib/cleaner_crm.ex (boundary exports) and router.ex (/quotes, /quotes/new, /quotes/:id).

Design: a quote is built entirely in LiveView socket state and only persisted at send time (freezing rate_cents/amount_cents into QuoteItem rows), so rate-card edits never touch sent quotes. Pricing is a pure module (no DB); Quoting.send_quote/3 refuses with :not_finalizable when any priced line item lacks a rate or total is 0. Money is a small top-level formatter module per the ADR. Quote has an optional client_id -> Clients.Client to honor the declared dependency, but the UI only exposes free-text client_name/phone (phone-lead flow) since no criterion needed a client picker.

One notable implementation snag worth flagging: Phoenix.LiveViewTest's form/3 validates every override key against the *currently rendered* DOM before the event is sent, so a field can't be conditionally removed from the DOM the same step it's being set. Fixed by always rendering all four model-specific inputs (never removed), toggling only visual hidden class + the data-test attribute based on the active model — the input's name stays live for scraping, has_element? only matches when data-test is present.

Pricing is a pure module (no DB); Quoting.send_quote/3 refuses with :not_finalizable when any priced line item lacks a rate or total is 0. Money is a small top-level formatter module per the ADR. Quote has an optional client_id -> Clients.Client to honor the declared dependency, but the UI only exposes free-text client_name/phone (phone-lead flow) since no criterion needed a client picker.

One notable implementation snag worth flagging: Phoenix.LiveViewTest's form/3 validates every override key against the *currently rendered* DOM before the event is sent, so a field can't be conditionally removed from the DOM the same step it's being set. I've completed the Quoting slice implementation and reported back to the team lead. Summary of the work:

**Implemented:**
- `lib/cleaner_crm/quoting.ex` — context with rate card and quote management, `send_quote/3` that freezes pricing at send time
- `lib/cleaner_crm/quoting/{quote,quote_item,rate_card,pricing}.ex` — schemas plus a pure `Pricing` module for computing totals
- `lib/cleaner_crm/money.ex` — the `$X.XX` formatting helper called for by the money-handling ADR
- `priv/repo/migrations/20260707200099_create_quoting_tables.exs`
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/quote_live/{index,builder}.ex` — the list view and the combined rate-card/quote builder
- Additive edits to `lib/cleaner_crm.ex` (boundary exports) and `router.ex` (`/quotes`, `/quotes/new`, `/quotes/:id`)

**Key design decision:** a quote lives entirely in LiveView state and is only persisted at the moment it's sent, freezing rates/amounts into `QuoteItem` rows so later rate-card edits never alter a sent quote.

**Verification:** All 6 story-835 spex scenarios pass (6/6 green), `mix compile` is clean, `mix format` is clean, and the full `mix test` suite shows 145 tests with 1 failure — a pre-existing arithmetic bug in another agent's `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.PayrollExport` module, unrelated to this work.

**Notable snag:** Phoenix.LiveViewTest's `form/3` validates every field you're setting against the currently-rendered DOM before submitting the event, so conditionally removing an input from the DOM the same step you're setting it breaks the test. I fixed this by always rendering all four model-specific inputs and toggling only a CSS `hidden` class plus the `data-test` attribute based on the active pricing model.

I also had to resolve migration timestamp collisions from other agents working concurrently on Billing/TimeTracking/Quality (pure renames, no content changes) since they were blocking all migrations, and reset the shared test database to reconcile schema state.
